text:
Montreal has controlled more of the play so far. At five on five, MTL has taken 55% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) while SJS sits at 45%. Over 60 minutes, MTL creates 3.32 expected goals and allows 3.4, against 2.88 and 3.8 for SJS, whose defense has been the bigger problem. The model projects 3.39 expected goals for MTL tonight and 3.03 for SJS. On special teams, SJS earns 0.74 expected goals per game on the power play and MTL 0.52, but MTL has taken 5.4 penalties a game, which keeps handing the other side chances. SJS is also on the second night of a back-to-back after a 3-1 loss in Toronto.

The goalie matchup runs against reputation. Alex Nedeljkovic (projected for SJS) has saved 4.22 goals above expected this season but was 2.06 below last year. Jakub Dobes (projected for MTL) is at -5.55 this season after a +17.26 year in 2025-26, and he has gone 1-2-1 with a .841 save percentage over his last four starts. Nedeljkovic starts over Yaroslav Askarov.

Form leans toward MTL as well. The Canadiens are 3-2-0 in their last five with 52% of the expected goals, and they won the chance battle in four of those games. The Sharks are 1-3-1 with 45%. The one standout is Macklin Celebrini, who has a 44% chance to score and an 84% chance to record a point, and he's on the top power play. For MTL, Cole Caufield (43% to score) is the one to watch, and Montreal is without Ivan Demidov.
